title_ar: قناة الرسالة تستضيف فضيلة الشيخ الددو حول فقه الخلاف والاختلاف
title_en: Al-Risalah Channel Hosts Sheikh al-Dedew on the Jurisprudence of Disagreement and Difference
body_ar: استضافت قناة الرسالة الفضائية فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء أمس الجمعة 28 جمادى الأولى 1433هـ الموافق: 20 إبريل 2012 في حلقة جديدة من برنامجها الأسبوعي "لقاء الجمعة" وهو برنامج ينقسم إلى ثلاث فقرات؛ تتعلق الأولى منها بنقاش حول موضوع الحلقة الذي كان "فقه الخلاف والاختلاف" بينما كانت الفقرة الثانية تعليقا من فضيلة الشيخ على أهم الأحداث التي شهدها العالم خلال أيام الأسبوع المنصرم، وكانت الفقرة الأخيرة إجابة من الشيخ على تساؤلات سجلتها القناة من الشارع المصري حول مواقفه من عدد من القضايا والإشكالات الراهنة وأنشطة الشيخ في بلده موريتانيا. وقد أكد الشيخ في حديثه على أن الخلاف منه ما هو سائغ يجوز تداوله، بينما تبقى ثوابت الشرع خارج نطاق الخلاف المسموح به، وذكر بحدود الخلاف، والقضايا التي يصح فيه الإنكار على المخالفين، منبها على ضرورة الحوار والجدال بالتي هي أحسن دون حدود حتى مع الكفار وفي قضايا الإلاهيات، ثم أجاب فضيلة الشيخ على عدد من الشبه المتعلقة بفضل الصحابة، وببعض أشراط الساعة، والتي يثير البعض بين الفينة والأخرى شبهات حولها. وفي الفقرة الثانية أعرب فضيلة الشيخ عن حرمة الاختطاف دون وجه حق، وضرورة احترام حرمات الغير وعدم التعرض لها إلا في الحدود التي أجازها الشرع، ثم أكد على حتمية نصر الإسلام في مختلف الأمصار والبلدان، وأدان زيارة المسجد الأقصى في ظل الاحتلال مهما كانت المسوغات، وفي نهاية الحلقة أجاب على تساؤلات الشارع التي بثت القناة عينات منها. وخلال إجابته أكد فضيلة الشيخ على عدم وجود الرق في موريتانيا، وقدم تعريفا بمركز تكوين العلماء الذي يرأسه، ونبه إلى أن العالم مرتبط بكل مكان يتعلق به حكم الله تعالى سواء كان المسجد أو البرلمان.
body_en:
The al-Risalah satellite channel hosted the eminent scholar Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, yesterday, Friday 28 Jumada al-Ula 1433 AH, corresponding to 20 April 2012, in a new episode of its weekly programme "The Friday Meeting". The programme is divided into three segments. The first of them concerns a discussion of the episode's subject, which was "The Jurisprudence of Disagreement and of Difference"; the second segment was a comment by the Sheikh on the most important events the world had witnessed during the days of the week just past; and the last segment was the Sheikh's answer to questions recorded by the channel from the Egyptian street about his positions on a number of current issues and difficulties, and about the Sheikh's activities in his own country, Mauritania.

In his talk the Sheikh affirmed that there is disagreement which is admissible and permissible to circulate, while the fixed certainties of the Sharia remain outside the scope of permitted disagreement. He recalled the limits of disagreement, and the questions in which it is valid to rebuke those who hold a different view, drawing attention to the necessity of dialogue and of disputing in the way that is best, without limits — even with the disbelievers, and in questions concerning the divine (ilāhiyyāt). The Sheikh then answered a number of the doubts raised concerning the merit of the Companions and concerning some of the portents of the Hour, about which some people stir up doubts from time to time.

In the second segment the Sheikh expressed that the abduction of a person without lawful right is forbidden (ḥarām), and the necessity of respecting what is inviolable in others and of not encroaching upon it except within the limits the Sharia has permitted. He then affirmed the inevitability of Islam's victory in the various provinces and countries, and condemned visiting the Aqsa Mosque under the occupation, whatever the justifications advanced; and at the end of the episode he answered the questions from the street, samples of which the channel had broadcast.

In the course of his answer the Sheikh affirmed that slavery does not exist in Mauritania, gave an introduction to the Centre for the Formation of Scholars which he heads, and pointed out that the scholar is bound to every place to which a ruling of God Most High attaches, whether that be the mosque or the parliament.

flags.arabic: أكد فضيلة الشيخ على عدم وجود الرق في موريتانيا
flags.context: the closing paragraph, in the Sheikh's answers to questions from the public
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12, and the single most sensitive sentence in this slice. The existence of slavery and its legacy in Mauritania is a matter of documented international concern and of active domestic litigation and politics; a flat denial of it, published in English under the Sheikh's name, would be read worldwide, would be quoted against him and against Ummah Collective, and could carry legal exposure. The sentence has been translated exactly as the source has it: neither softened nor strengthened, and with no qualification added. Note what the source does and does not establish: this is one clause of a news desk's summary of a television answer, with no record of the question asked, no indication whether he was speaking of the legal status of slavery, its formal abolition, or the factual situation, and no recording in the corpus. Publication is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office to decide, and should not happen without the recording.

flags.arabic: وأدان زيارة المسجد الأقصى في ظل الاحتلال مهما كانت المسوغات
flags.context: the Sheikh's comment on the events of the week
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. A position on a contested political-religious question of the day. 'أدان' is rendered 'condemned', which is its ordinary force; note that the source reports a condemnation and not a ruling, and no ruling word appears — nothing here may be rendered as ḥarām or as any of the five rulings. 'مهما كانت المسوغات' is rendered 'whatever the justifications advanced' and its absoluteness kept.

flags.context: one sentence using the root ḥ-r-m in two different senses
options: render the first as 'is forbidden (ḥarām)' and the second as 'what is inviolable'
flags.note: HOMONYM WARNING, and the two senses stand in a single clause. حرمة as a verbal noun is the state of being forbidden — a ruling on an act, and the fixed rendering 'forbidden (ḥarām)' applies. حرمات in the plural are the inviolable things of a person: life, honour, property. Rendering both alike would either turn a statement about people's inviolability into a prohibition or dissolve a ruling into a sentiment. Note also that 'دون وجه حق' qualifies the first: the report has him forbidding abduction without lawful right, and says nothing about abduction with it.

flags.arabic: الخلاف منه ما هو سائغ يجوز تداوله
flags.context: the core of the episode's subject
options: there is disagreement which is admissible and permissible to circulate
some disagreement is tolerable and may be discussed
some difference is within bounds and it is allowed to air it
flags.note: يجوز is the verbal form of jāʾiz and is rendered 'permissible', consistent with mubāḥ in the fixed mapping; the record gives no ground to read it as anything stronger or weaker. But this is the whole of what the corpus holds on the episode's announced subject. The limits of legitimate disagreement, the 'fixed certainties' that lie outside it, and the questions in which rebuke is valid are all named and none is specified. A reader will want to know where the line falls and the record does not say. Must not be displayed as a statement of his position on the substance.

flags.arabic: العالم مرتبط بكل مكان يتعلق به حكم الله تعالى سواء كان المسجد أو البرلمان
flags.context: the final clause of the record
options: the scholar (al-ʿālim) is bound to every place to which a ruling of God attaches
the world (al-ʿālam) is bound to every place to which a ruling of God attaches
flags.note: The Arabic is unvocalised and the two readings differ entirely. 'The scholar' is adopted: the sentence follows an account of his scholarly centre, it contrasts the mosque with the parliament, and the claim it makes — that a scholar's concern reaches wherever God's ruling reaches, including politics — is intelligible and consequential, while the other reading is not. This is nonetheless an inference from context and should be checked against the recording. Note that the sentence, on this reading, is a defence of scholarly engagement in politics and belongs with the editorial-review material above.

flags.arabic: الجدال بالتي هي أحسن ... حتى مع الكفار وفي قضايا الإلاهيات
options: disputing in the way that is best — even with the disbelievers, and in questions concerning the divine (ilāhiyyāt)
arguing in the better way, even with unbelievers and on theological questions
flags.note: 'بالتي هي أحسن' is the wording of Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:125 and of Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:46, used here without quotation marks or citation; the English keeps the source's unmarked form. ilāhiyyāt is the division of theology treating God's essence and attributes — the province of the kalām terms in style guide section 8, not of the five legal rulings; the term is not in the glossary and is bracketed. Note the striking claim that the duty of best-manner dialogue holds 'without limits' even there.

translator_notes: A news-desk summary of a televised interview. Every position attributed to the Sheikh here is at second hand, in a clause or two, with the question that prompted it absent. Four separate matters in this record would each be a full fatwa if the corpus held one.
The CMS timestamp, 21 April 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the broadcast to Friday 20 April 2012.

'ثوابت الشرع' is rendered 'the fixed certainties of the Sharia' — the settled matters not open to disagreement. The term is not in the glossary and would be worth adding: it recurs across this corpus and carries weight.
'أشراط الساعة' is rendered 'the portents of the Hour', the established English for the signs preceding the end of the world.
dec: Carries the same flat denial that slavery exists in Mauritania, on a subject of documented international concern and active domestic litigation.
